JPMANN provides retaining wall design for residential and commercial developments, excavations, basements, infrastructure projects, and sites with changes in ground level. Our engineers assess soil conditions, groundwater, structural loads, retained height, wall movement, nearby structures, and construction requirements to develop suitable retaining wall systems.

Our retaining wall solutions address the specific demands of each site. We consider earth pressure, surcharge loads, groundwater, foundation conditions, and construction constraints when developing the design. The approach helps provide effective wall retention while supporting ground stability and controlled excavation.

Different retaining wall systems suit different project conditions. JPMANN designs reinforced concrete walls, piled retaining walls, contiguous piled walls, and secant piled walls based on the required depth, loading, available space, and ground conditions.

Our engineers coordinate the retaining wall design with foundation, excavation, and wider structural requirements. This integrated approach helps ensure the proposed system works effectively with the surrounding ground and other elements of the project.
How Do Retaining Walls Work?
Retaining walls resist the horizontal pressure created by retained soil. The wall transfers these forces through its structural elements and foundation or embedded support system.
Effective wall retention starts with an understanding of the ground. Soil properties, groundwater levels, ground layers, and existing foundations influence how the retained ground behaves.
Ground Investigation

Ground investigation provides important information for retaining wall design. Engineers use soil strength, stiffness, groundwater levels, and ground conditions to establish suitable design parameters.
Existing site information also helps identify nearby foundations, services, structures, and other constraints that could affect the retaining wall.
Structural and Stability Design

Retaining wall calculations assess the forces acting on the structure and confirm the required stability. Design checks include sliding, overturning, bearing pressure, structural capacity, lateral resistance, and overall stability.

Groundwater also requires careful consideration because water pressure increases the forces acting on a retaining wall. Appropriate drainage and groundwater control measures form part of the design where required.
Retaining Wall Solutions

JPMANN develops retaining wall solutions according to the requirements of each site. Wall height, soil conditions, groundwater, loading, excavation depth, access, and nearby structures all influence the engineering approach.

Reinforced concrete retaining walls provide a permanent solution for many changes in ground level. Piled retaining walls provide deeper support where excavation or site constraints require an embedded system.

Contiguous piled walls use closely spaced piles to retain ground during excavation. Secant piled walls use overlapping piles to create a more continuous retaining structure and suit projects where ground retention and groundwater conditions require greater wall continuity.
King post systems provide another approach for selected excavation and retention requirements. The final retaining wall system is selected after assessing the ground and structural conditions.
Benefits of Professional Retaining Wall Design
Professional retaining wall design provides a controlled engineering solution for changes in ground level and excavation.
Key benefits include:
• Improved ground stability through engineered lateral support
• Controlled excavation where conventional slopes are not practical
• Reduced risk of excessive ground movement near existing structures
• Efficient use of restricted development sites
• Appropriate management of soil and groundwater pressures
• Clear structural requirements for construction teams
A properly designed retaining wall also supports coordination between geotechnical, structural, architectural, and construction teams.
Why Choose JPMANN?

JPMANN combines geotechnical and structural engineering knowledge when developing retaining wall systems. Our engineers assess the interaction between the structure and surrounding ground rather than treating the wall as an isolated structural element.

Each retaining wall design responds to the specific project conditions. Our process considers retained height, soil parameters, groundwater, surcharge loading, nearby structures, excavation requirements, and construction sequence.
Project Experience

JPMANN has experience with complex ground retention and foundation projects. A project at New Road in Chatham involved a contiguous piled wall with varying retained heights. The design considered pile spacing, pile depth, and reinforcement to develop an appropriate retaining solution.
This project demonstrates the importance of project specific engineering when ground retention requirements vary across a site.
Where Are Retaining Walls Used?

Retaining walls support a wide range of construction and infrastructure projects. Residential developments often require retaining structures around extensions, gardens, driveways, boundaries, and changes in ground level.

Commercial developments use retaining wall systems for basements, car parks, excavation boundaries, and constrained sites. Infrastructure projects also use retaining structures where roads, utilities, rail works, or other assets require changes in ground level.
Common applications include:
• Residential developments
• Commercial buildings
• Basement construction

• Infrastructure projects
• Urban developments
• Excavation support
• Sites with significant changes in ground level
Our Retaining Wall Design Process
JPMANN follows a structured design process that links ground conditions with structural requirements.

The process begins with a review of available drawings, site information, ground investigation data, and project requirements. Engineers then assess soil conditions, groundwater, retained height, surcharge loads, nearby structures, and construction constraints.

The design team identifies suitable retaining wall systems and completes the required geotechnical and structural calculations. Stability, structural capacity, lateral resistance, groundwater effects, and wall movement are assessed as part of the design.
The final engineering information supports construction planning and coordination with the wider project team.
Retaining Walls and Ground Investigation
Ground investigation plays an important role in retaining wall design. Soil strength and stiffness affect earth pressure, wall movement, foundation resistance, and overall stability.
Groundwater conditions also influence the design. Water pressure behind a retaining wall adds load and requires suitable drainage or groundwater control measures.

JPMANN uses available ground investigation information to establish suitable design parameters. Where information is limited, our engineers identify additional investigation requirements needed to support the design.
Frequently Asked Questions
What Are Retaining Walls Used For?

Retaining walls hold back soil where different ground levels exist. Retaining wall systems support excavations, basements, roads, boundaries, infrastructure, and developments on sloping sites. Engineers design the structure to resist soil pressure, surcharge loads, groundwater pressure, and other forces affecting stability.
What Retaining Wall System Is Best?

The best retaining wall system depends on ground conditions, retained height, groundwater, loading, available space, and construction requirements. Reinforced concrete walls, piled retaining walls, contiguous piled walls, secant piled walls, and king post systems suit different site conditions. Engineers select the appropriate system after assessing the project requirements.
Do Retaining Walls Need Structural Calculations?

Retaining walls require engineering calculations where structural stability and ground retention form part of the construction works. Calculations assess sliding, overturning, bearing pressure, structural capacity, soil pressure, groundwater effects, and overall stability. The required design depends on the wall type and project conditions.
What Information Is Needed for Retaining Wall Design?

Retaining wall design requires information about ground conditions, retained height, groundwater, nearby structures, surcharge loads, site constraints, and construction requirements. Ground investigation provides important soil parameters for engineering calculations. Existing drawings and information about neighbouring foundations also help establish suitable design conditions.
What Is Wall Retention?

Wall retention describes the ability of a structure to retain soil and resist lateral ground pressure. Engineers assess wall retention through soil pressure calculations, structural capacity, embedment, foundation resistance, lateral support, and overall stability. Groundwater and surcharge loads also affect the required retention capacity.
What Are Retaining Wall Solutions for Deep Excavations?

Retaining wall solutions for deep excavations include piled retaining walls, contiguous piled walls, secant piled walls, and other engineered support systems. The appropriate solution depends on excavation depth, soil conditions, groundwater, nearby structures, available space, and construction sequence.
Can an Existing Retaining Wall Be Assessed?

An existing retaining wall can be assessed by reviewing its condition, geometry, construction, ground conditions, drainage, loading, and observed movement. Engineering assessment determines whether the structure provides suitable capacity for existing or proposed conditions and identifies requirements for repair, strengthening, or replacement.
How Do Retaining Walls Manage Groundwater?

Retaining walls manage groundwater through appropriate drainage and groundwater control measures. Design considers groundwater levels and water pressure acting on the structure. Drainage requirements depend on the wall system, soil conditions, excavation depth, and project requirements.
Are Retaining Walls Required for Basement Construction?

Basement construction often requires a retaining wall because excavation creates a difference in ground level. The retaining system provides support during excavation and may form part of the permanent basement structure. Engineers assess soil conditions, groundwater, nearby buildings, and excavation depth when selecting the appropriate solution.

Frequently Asked Questions
What does a structural engineer do?

A structural engineer designs, assesses and analyses buildings and other structures to ensure they are safe, stable and compliant with UK Building Regulations. Structural engineers calculate how loads are transferred through a building and recommend appropriate structural solutions for new developments, extensions, alterations and refurbishments.
When do I need a structural engineer in London?

You may require a structural engineer if you are planning a house extension, loft conversion, basement excavation, removing a load-bearing wall, constructing a new property or making significant structural alterations. A structural engineer may also be required when investigating structural movement, subsidence or defects within an existing building.
Do I need structural calculations for Building Regulations?

Yes. Many construction projects require structural calculations to demonstrate that the proposed structural elements comply with current Building Regulations. These calculations are typically submitted to Building Control as part of the approval process and help ensure the safety and stability of the completed structure.
Can you design steel beams for house extensions?

Yes. Our structural engineers design steel beams and supporting structural elements for house extensions, loft conversions, wall removals and refurbishment projects. Every beam is individually designed based on the building's structural requirements rather than using standard sizes.
Do you work with architects and contractors?

Yes. We regularly collaborate with architects, developers, contractors, planning consultants and Building Control officers throughout London. Early collaboration helps integrate structural engineering into the overall project design, reducing delays and improving construction efficiency.
Can you inspect structural cracks in my property?

Yes. We undertake structural inspections to investigate cracking, movement, settlement and other signs of structural distress. Following the inspection, we provide professional advice and, where required, recommend appropriate remedial measures.
Do older London properties require structural assessments before alterations?

In many cases, yes. London contains a large number of Victorian, Edwardian and Georgian properties that may require detailed structural assessment before extensions or alterations are undertaken. Understanding the condition of the existing structure helps ensure that proposed works can be carried out safely and efficiently.
Do you provide structural engineering services for commercial developments?

Yes. We provide structural engineering consultancy for a wide range of commercial projects, including office buildings, retail developments, industrial facilities, apartment schemes, educational buildings and mixed-use developments throughout London.
Can you assist with foundation design?

Yes. Foundation design forms an important part of our structural engineering service. We work alongside geotechnical specialists to assess site conditions before designing foundation solutions that are appropriate for the proposed structure and ground conditions.
Which areas of London do you cover?

JP Mann provides structural engineering services throughout Greater London, including Central London, Westminster, Camden, Kensington, Chelsea, Islington, Southwark, Greenwich, Croydon, Barnet, Ealing, Richmond, Hammersmith, Hackney, Tower Hamlets and the surrounding boroughs.
